- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending down.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in the 10–20 day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2 week “recovery” phase after dip; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment turns positive after dip.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term momentum; dampen forecast volatility by 15–25% in next 7 days.
